parameters.query:
UPDATE incidents
SET token_used = true
WHERE id = $1
  AND approval_token = $2
  AND status = 'awaiting_approval'
  AND expires_at > now()
  AND token_used = false
RETURNING id, diagnosis_json, workflow_id, workflow_name, node_name;

parameters.responseBody:
⚠️ Invalid or Expired Link

This approval link is no longer valid. It may have expired (48h) or already been used.

✅ Decision Received

Processing your decision. You'll get a WhatsApp message with the result shortly.

parameters.command:
=flock -w 300 /var/lock/heal.lock -c '
cd /home/victor-ferrareto-dias/projects/n8n-self-healing && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only && \
git checkout -B fix/incident-{{ $("Prepare Fix Incident File").item.json.incident_id }} && \
claude -p "$(cat prompts/fix.md)" \
  --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob,Edit,Write,Bash(git:*),Bash(gh pr create:*)" \
  --output-format json --max-turns 40'

parameters.query:
UPDATE incidents
SET status = CASE WHEN $1 = 'pr_created' THEN 'pr_open' ELSE 'failed_healing' END,
    pr_url = $2
WHERE id = $3;
UPDATE incidents SET status = 'rejected' WHERE id = $1;

parameters.content:
ATOMIC CONSUME: single UPDATE that only succeeds if id+token match,
status is still awaiting_approval, not expired, AND token_used=false —
sets token_used=true in the same statement. Prevents double-click from
triggering Phase 2 twice (DB serializes concurrent writes).

ASYNC PATTERN: "Respond to Webhook" answers the browser immediately
("processing..."), but the workflow keeps running after it — Phase 2
can take minutes and the browser would time out waiting.

PHASE 2 (write mode): on a dedicated branch (never touches main),
allowedTools now includes Edit/Write/Bash(git:*)/Bash(gh pr create:*).
If the approved fix turns out empty/inapplicable, it ABORTS and reports
rather than improvising — verified live in testing.

Reject path: just marks the incident as rejected — no Claude Code
call, no branch, nothing else happens.

json.abort_reason: The target file workflows/qfPih1jqBdVqoZ3v.json does not exist on main or on fix/incident-40 (the branch this Phase 2 task is running on) — it was removed in commit 2fe8252 ('drop unrelated workflow exports') and only still exists on the stale, unmerged branch fix/incident-29 (HEAD 13bd3e3). There is nothing to apply the fix to in the current scope. The Phase 1 diagnosis itself flags this and states a human must decide where the fix should land (re-add the file to main from fix/incident-29, or apply the fix directly on that branch) before Phase 2 can proceed. Improvising by resurrecting the file here would go beyond the approved fix, so aborting per instructions.
